messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: GeoDNS anomalies detected — surge of NXDOMAIN / inconsistent answers for api.redwood-inference.com from APAC resolvers. Impact: increased 5xx and client reconnections for customers in ap-southeast-1 and ap-northeast-1. Priority P1. Paging sara (oncall).

sara (oncall): I’m on it. seeing alerts: latency + error spike from our inference edge pool in ap-southeast-1. Any initial probe links?

miguel (cloudops): posting probes: dig from probe cluster (ap-sg1):
```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 2
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.redwood-inference.com. IN A
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood-inference.com. 60 IN SOA ns-1.aws-route53.com. hostmaster 2026031501 7200 900 1209600 86400
```
Multiple probes show AUTHORITY but no A/AAAA answers, some return NXDOMAIN from certain public resolvers (1.1.1.1 shows answers, 8.8.8.8 returns NXDOMAIN intermittently).

jay (networks): traceroute from a failing client to our edge returns nothing — looks like resolver-level mismatch between Cloudflare edge resolvers and Route53 geo answers. Checked Route53 geo records: ap-southeast-1-targets are still healthy, health checks OK. But I can reproduce inconsistent answers when querying from Cloudflare resolver ASN ranges.

sara (oncall): hypothesis: GeoDNS routing updates not propagating consistently to external resolvers, maybe due to recent zone change + low TTL. What changed recently in DNS?

kelsey (prod-sre): We rolled a geo DNS change ~30m ago to adjust weighting for ap-southeast-1 during traffic shift. TTL was 60s. Could be propagation oscillation under high query volume.

miguel (cloudops): Escalating to registrar/provider? Also seeing Route53 query latency spikes in ap-east-1 zone. Opening AWS ticket but need on-the-wire mitigation now.

alice (customer-ops): Customers reporting higher tail latency and intermittent 502s in APAC. One enterprise customer opened a Sev ticket. We should update status page.

sara (oncall): Agreed — immediate steps: 1) Roll back recent geo-weight change to previous stable config; 2) Increase TTL to 300s to reduce oscillation while we stabilize; 3) Add a static fallback A record (short-circuit geo) that returns healthy global IPs for affected regions if geo lookup fails; 4) Notify status. Who can perform Route53 change now?

miguel (cloudops): I can do the Route53 rollback and TTL bump. Will use our internal dnsctl tool. Commands:
```
# rollback geo policy
dnsctl sets geo-policy redwood-inference.com --policy previous --commit
# set default TTL
dnsctl set-ttl redwood-inference.com 300 --apply
# add fallback
dnsctl add-record api.redwood-inference.com A 3.120.45.78 --zone redwood-inference.com --comment "fallback for inconsistent resolvers"
```
Applying now, will post logs.

incident-bot: Action logged: rollout.start by miguel at 1775551300. Change set id: cs-89234.

miguel (cloudops): Done. Rollback and TTL increase applied (cs-89234). Added fallback A record. Waiting for propagation.

jay (networks): Running external queries from Cloudflare and Google again:
```
# cloudflare resolver (1.1.1.1)
dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com +short
3.120.45.78
# google resolver (8.8.8.8)
dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com +short
; sometimes blank / NXDOMAIN
```
It looks like 1.1.1.1 started returning the fallback IP, 8.8.8.8 still flapping. Might be cache TTLs.

sara (oncall): Start rolling traffic to fallback IP in our edge LB for APAC so services don’t see DNS flaps. Miguel, can you add the fallback IP to the APAC pool?

miguel (cloudops): adding to apac-lb pool now:
```
infractl lb add-backend apac-lb 3.120.45.78 --weight 50 --healthcheck http:/healthz
```
Done. Health checks green.

kelsey (prod-sre): Observability: errors dropping ~40% within 3m of LB change; tail latency improving. Still seeing occasional client retries. Post-change metrics: 5xxs down, p95 latency for ap-southeast-1 from 1.2s -> 0.35s.

alice (customer-ops): Status page update drafted: "We are investigating DNS resolution issues affecting some APAC users; mitigation in progress. Customers may observe intermittent errors or higher latency."
status-bot: Posted to status page (INC-APAC-DNS-177555).

sara (oncall): Good. Next: keep monitoring for 30m, liaise with AWS support to verify if Route53 zone is stable and whether any backend issues. Also open Cloudflare support ticket to check resolver caching behavior for geo answers. Jay, can you DM CF rep?

jay (networks): On it. DM sent to CF escalation, included dig outputs and cs-89234.

miguel (cloudops): AWS case opened: case #AWS-776543. Noted Route53 spikes and possible internal throttling affecting geo answer propagation. AWS acknowledged and investigating.

sara (oncall): If AWS confirms propagation delays we should consider switching authoritative name servers to secondary provider temporarily (we have pre-provisioned NS at ns2.cf-dns) — but that’s disruptive. Keep as fallback only.

kelsey (prod-sre): Also tracking customer impact: 7 customers reported degraded experience, 2 enterprise have active support tickets. Marking ongoing customer impact: degraded in APAC.

alice (customer-ops): I've messaged the two enterprise contacts with ETA: "mitigation in progress; next update in 30 minutes". They acknowledged.

incident-bot: Reminder: if this remains P1 after 60m escalate to incident commander. 1775551599 (60m timer set).

sara (oncall): Acknowledged. Continuing monitoring. If errors remain >5% escalate.

--- 18 minutes later ---

miguel (cloudops): AWS says they observed a backend replication lag affecting geo DNS records for a small subset of resolver prefixes — propagation delay up to ~2m per edge, causing inconsistent answers. AWS recommends keeping TTL longer and avoiding frequent geo policy toggles during high QPS. They've marked the underlying event as resolved but recommend we keep fallback in place for 1 hour.

jay (networks): Cloudflare replied: they cache negative responses differently across POPs; some POPs had cached NXDOMAIN due to earlier queries and will honor the negative cache TTL. Suggested we push a DNS refresh by issuing increasing SOA serial? Not ideal. They also cleared cache on their side for our zone per ticket.

kelsey (prod-sre): Metrics: errors now below 2% and trending down. Rolling risk to watch.

sara (oncall): OK — decision: keep fallback record and LB addition for 1 hour, then remove fallback after 60m if stable. Keep TTL at 300 for 2 hours, then revert to normal 60 only once all providers confirm healthy propagation. Update status page with mitigation summary.

alice (customer-ops): Updated enterprise contacts with mitigation and AWS/CF confirmation. One customer asked for postmortem once resolved.

incident-bot: Action logged: mitigation.complete? Not yet — pending watch window.

--- Handoff ---

sara (oncall): Handoff notes for night oncall (miguel2):
- Incident: GeoDNS inconsistent answers affected APAC (thread 1775551234)
- Actions taken: rolled back geo-policy, increased TTL to 300s, added fallback A record 3.120.45.78, added to apac LB pool, notified AWS/Cloudflare and status updated.
- Current state: errors <2%, watching until 1775551999 then remove fallback if stable.
- Followups: AWS case #AWS-776543, CF ticket #CF-99321, create postmortem focusing on geo-policy churn + TTL strategy.

miguel (cloudops): Acknowledged handoff. Will continue watch and remove fallback at 1775551999 if metrics stable.

kelsey (prod-sre): Add action item: automate rate-limiting of geo-policy changes and gate TTLs for geo records.

status-bot: Final update to status page: "Mitigation deployed; traffic rerouted to fallback IP while DNS propagation stabilized. Customers may still see intermittent issues; monitoring continues."

sara (oncall): Thanks team. Postmortem draft please include timeline, exact DNS edits, why rollback was needed, and customer impact table. :eyes:

alice (customer-ops): Noted. Will collate customer tickets and include impact statements.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active work; will reopen if alerts reappear."
